_comment: Single source of truth for trusted networks / Proxmox IPSets. Consumers: ansible proxmox_firewall (templates cluster.fw IPSETs), ansible group_vars (trusted nets → crowdsec_whitelist_cidrs), nix krg.firewall (monitoring source, service SSH restriction). Edit here only. Lives under nix/ because the flake can only read its own subtree. monitoring_host = the IP that runs Prometheus and scrapes the node/ipmi exporters (currently krg-prod, which hosts the monitoring compose stack). NOTE ON `ops`: those are per-admin RESIDENTIAL addresses and they change when a router restarts (chris's moved twice in 2026-08-18..20, the second time after a power outage). Symptom is distinctive: port 22 TIMES OUT while DSM web still answers 200 — dropped, not down — so suspect this before suspecting the host. REPLACE a stale entry, never append: an address you no longer hold gets reassigned to another customer, and appending would leave a stranger holding an SSH allow into the fleet. `ops` gates SSH via nix sshSources, the cluster.fw IPSets below and the synology_security prepends, so one stale line is a fleet-wide lockout, not a single-host one. DELIBERATE DECISION (2026-08-20, chris): keep these as single /32s and DO NOT widen to an ISP prefix. The occasional lockout is the accepted cost; a broader allow is a permanently larger attack surface, and these addresses have spanned three different /16s, so no sane prefix would cover them anyway. Fix by updating the value, not the mask. Do NOT add explanatory keys inside `ipsets` — cluster.fw.j2 iterates it with .items() and would render a bogus IPSet.
